newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq export outlets can handle 2.4 mln bpd - official.
newsitem.headline: Iraq export outlets can handle 2.4 mln bpd - official.

text.p: Iraq's export outlets are currently capable of handling 2.4 million barrels of oil per day (bpd) almost three times the amount Baghdad will be allowed to export under its food-for-oil deal with U.N., a senior Iraqi oil official said on Tuesday.
"Mina al-Bakr is ready one hundred percent. Through it we can export 1.2 million bpd," Taha Hmud Mosa senior under-secretary of Iraq's oil ministry told Reuters.
"Through the second outlet via Ceyhan in Turkey we can export also about 1.2 million bpd," he said.

He said Iraq intended to use both outlets simultaneously once the United Nations gives it the go-ahead to start the exports under the partial export deal whose conditions Baghdad accepted on November 25.
The scheme, designed to ease the suffering of the Iraqi people under U.N. trade sanctions, allows Baghdad $2 billion of exports in six months.
Mosa said Iraq intended to ship about 350,000 bpd via Mina al-Bakr on the Gulf and an estimated 450,000 bpd through Turkey depending on world oil prices.
He said the export capacity of Gulf terminals could be raised to 1.6 million bpd "in the near future after the completion of certain requirements."

Mosa said Iraq was also planning to regain the original capacity of its twin pipeline via Turkey of 1.6 million bpd. "One of the main (pumping) stations was bombed. This station can be restored in a few months and the capacity boosted to 1.6 million," he said.
